<!-- Page: docs/Plans/Emergent Capabilities -->
Source: docs/Plans/Emergent%20Capabilities/

# Emergent Capabilities

Capabilities that the naked objects architecture makes possible at the framework level.

**Status:** a list of candidates, not a plan. Each candidate now has a home, so this page can become a docs page about the pattern once they're placed:

| Candidate | Where it goes |
| --- | --- |
| Undo / redo | Its own plan when wanted, built on slot-change notifications and `pool.transaction()` |
| Search & filtering | [Tile Container Views](docs/Plans/Tile%20Container%20Views/) (container chrome, and search over windowed collections) |
| Data validation | [JSON Schema](docs/Plans/JSON%20Schema/) (validation against the same annotations) |
| Automated testing | An idea until wanted |
| Analytics & telemetry | An idea until wanted |
| Debug inspection | Already true; belongs in [Inspectors and Debugging](docs/Inspectors%20and%20Debugging/) |
| Migration & schema evolution | Its own plan, with the [Meta Plan](docs/Plans/Meta%20Plan/)'s note, when a slot type change needs it |

## Context

In a conventional web framework, cross-cutting concerns -- accessibility, internationalization, search, undo -- must be implemented per component. The cost scales linearly with the number of components, and coverage is always incomplete.

STRVCT's architecture inverts this. All state lives in typed slots with rich metadata (type, description, min/max, required, read-only). All UI passes through a small set of view classes (~15 tile and container classes render every application). This means a capability implemented once at the framework level automatically covers every application built on the framework.

Two capabilities already demonstrate this pattern:

- **[Accessibility](docs/Accessibility/)** -- Slot metadata maps to ARIA attributes, view classes emit roles and states, and every application inherits WCAG 2.2 AA support without per-component accessibility code.
- **[Internationalization](docs/Internationalization/)** -- Translatable nodes and a batched translation service give every application multilingual support through the model layer.

The candidates below are additional capabilities that the same architectural properties make possible. Each would be difficult or impractical to add after the fact in a conventional framework, but in STRVCT they can be implemented at the framework level and applied uniformly.

## Candidates

### Undo / Redo

Every state change flows through `didUpdateSlot()` with both old and new values. A command history captured at the slot level would give automatic undo/redo to every editable field and action. The notification system already provides the hook points; what's missing is a journal that records slot mutations and can replay them in reverse.

The slot system's granularity is an advantage here -- each undo step corresponds to a single slot change with a known previous value, avoiding the complexity of diffing arbitrary state trees.

### Search & Filtering

The entire node graph is structured, typed, and labeled. A framework-level search could traverse all nodes and slots, using slot metadata (type, description) to build both full-text and structured queries -- without per-component indexing code.

Slot types inform how to search (string matching on text slots, range queries on numeric slots, boolean filtering on flags), and node titles and descriptions provide natural result labels. The same traversal could support filtering a tile container's visible subnodes by query.

### Data Validation

Slot annotations already drive three consumers: JSON Schema for AI tool calls, ARIA attributes for screen readers, and persistence constraints. A fourth consumer -- a validation layer -- would use the same metadata (type, min, max, required, pattern) to provide automatic error messages and visual feedback on invalid input.

Because the metadata is already there, validation rules wouldn't need to be declared separately from the slot definitions. A field tile with `setAnnotation("minimum", 0)` would automatically reject negative input and display an appropriate message, just as it already emits `aria-valuemin="0"` and `"minimum": 0` in JSON Schema.

**Built 2026-11-17** as `slot.setMinimum(0)` and its siblings: see [JSON Schema](docs/Plans/JSON%20Schema/#what-was-built).

### Automated Testing

The model is effectively its own specification. Slot metadata declares what types, ranges, and constraints each field accepts. This makes generative testing possible: the framework could automatically produce test cases for every editable slot (valid and invalid input for its type), exercise every action, and walk every navigation path in the node graph.

This is a stronger property than conventional snapshot or integration testing -- the tests derive from the model's structural definition rather than from manually written expectations, so they stay in sync as the model evolves.

### Analytics & Telemetry

Every user interaction passes through the same tile, navigation, and action paths. Instrumenting once at the framework level would capture usage data (which nodes are visited, which fields edited, which actions taken, how users navigate the hierarchy) for every application -- without per-feature tracking code.

The node hierarchy provides natural grouping for analytics events, and slot metadata provides labels and types for structured event properties.

### Debug Inspection

STRVCT applications are already their own inspectors -- the node hierarchy is directly navigable, every slot's current value is visible in the UI, and the notification system shows the flow of changes in real time. This isn't a feature to build; it's an inherent property of the naked objects pattern worth calling out as a capability.

Conventional frameworks require separate developer tools (React DevTools, Vue DevTools) to inspect component state. In STRVCT, the production UI and the debug inspector are the same thing.

### Migration & Schema Evolution

When slot definitions change across versions, the framework knows both the stored schema (from the persisted record) and the current schema (from live slot definitions). This structural knowledge makes automatic migration possible: detecting renamed, added, or removed slots and transforming stored records to match the current definition.

In conventional systems, schema migration requires manually written migration scripts. In STRVCT, the slot system provides enough information to detect and potentially automate many common migrations.

## The Common Pattern

Each candidate above follows the same structural argument:

1. **Slot metadata already describes the data** -- types, constraints, descriptions, and relationships are declared once in `initPrototypeSlots()`.
2. **A small set of view classes renders everything** -- behavior added to the ~15 tile and container classes covers every application.
3. **The notification system provides hook points** -- `didUpdateSlot()`, `scheduleSyncToView()`, and the notification center make it possible to intercept and react to changes at the framework level.
4. **The node hierarchy provides structure** -- traversal, search, serialization, and inspection all operate on a uniform graph rather than an ad-hoc component tree.

The cost of each capability is proportional to the number of view classes (small and fixed), not the number of application components (large and growing). This is the fundamental leverage of the naked objects pattern.


---

<!-- Page: docs/Plans/Graph Database -->
Source: docs/Plans/Graph%20Database/

# Graph Database

Long-term direction: replacing the current cloud storage backend with a native graph database.

**Status:** direction, no work planned (2026-11-13). The Record Store already provides per-record sync, change feeds by version and placement queries, and windowed collections cover large folders. See [Timeline](docs/Plans/Graph%20Database/#timeline) for what would make it compelling.

## Context

STRVCT's domain model is a cyclic graph of objects connected by typed references. Locally, this graph is stored in IndexedDB as a flat key-value map of serialized records, with object references represented as persistent unique IDs (puuids). In the cloud the same records are stored one per Firestore document, grouped into pools (one per document, each with a version), with folders formed by placing each pool's root row under its folder; edits are sent as versioned commits of the changed records (see [Cloud Object Pools](docs/Persistence/Cloud%20Object%20Pools/)). This record store already gives per-record sync, change feeds by version, and placement queries — much of what is listed below.

What remains is a mismatch at the level of references: the domain model is a graph, while the record store sees each reference only as an id inside a serialized payload. It can list a node's placed children, but it cannot answer structural queries across references or serve a subgraph by traversal.

## Why a Graph Database

A graph database would store nodes and edges as first-class entities, directly mirroring how the domain model already works internally:

**Structural alignment.** Each domain object becomes a node in the database. Each slot that references another object becomes an edge. The database's structure matches the application's structure — no serialization/deserialization impedance mismatch.

**Granular sync.** Changes to a single node or edge can be synced independently without uploading an entire pool snapshot or maintaining a separate delta log. Updating a contact's phone number doesn't require re-uploading the entire address book.

**Lazy traversal.** The database can serve subgraphs on demand — fetch a node and its immediate neighbors, then expand as the user navigates. This is the graph-native version of what collection sync's manifest stubs approximate with per-item lazy loading.

**Query by structure.** "Find all contacts who share a company with this person" or "show me every group this contact belongs to" become native graph traversals rather than full-table scans or application-level filtering.

**Conflict resolution at the edge level.** When two clients modify different parts of the same graph concurrently, a graph-aware system can merge at the node/edge level rather than the document level, reducing false conflicts.

## Prior Art

[vertex.js](https://github.com/stevedekorte/vertex.js) is an earlier graph database implementation by the framework author. It stores a persistent graph of nodes with named slots (key-value pairs), where values can be primitives or references to other nodes. The data model is close to what STRVCT's domain objects already look like:

- Nodes have unique IDs and named properties
- Properties can hold primitive values or references to other nodes
- The graph supports cycles and bidirectional traversal
- Queries walk the graph by following named edges

The concepts from vertex.js — persistent graph nodes with slot-based properties, structural traversal, and path-based addressing — map directly onto STRVCT's existing object model.

## What This Would Replace

The current cloud sync stack has several layers that a graph database would subsume:

| Current | Graph DB equivalent |
|---|---|
| JSON serialization of object records | Direct node/edge storage |
| puuid-based references between objects | Native graph edges |
| Per-record versioned commits | Per-node/per-edge mutations |
| Placement queries and windowed loading | Subgraph traversal |
| Changes since a pool version | Change feed on individual nodes/edges |
| Optimistic per-pool version checks | Node-level or edge-level conflict resolution |

The local IndexedDB layer would likely remain as a client-side cache, but the canonical store would be the graph database rather than the records collection.

## Challenges

### Scalability

A hosted graph database must handle concurrent reads and writes from many clients, with low latency for the interactive traversals that drive STRVCT's navigation-based UI. This is a harder operational problem than serving static JSON files from cloud storage.

### Partial sync and offline-first

STRVCT applications work offline with local data, syncing when connectivity returns. A graph database sync protocol needs to handle:

- Efficient diffing: which nodes/edges changed since last sync?
- Subgraph boundaries: which parts of the graph does this client care about?
- Conflict resolution: two clients modified the same node offline — how to merge?

### Migration

Existing applications store data in the records collection. A migration path is needed — likely a period where both backends coexist, with the graph database gradually taking over as the primary store.

### Hosting and operations

Firestore is a managed service with minimal operational overhead. A graph database requires either a managed graph DB service (e.g., Neo4j Aura, Amazon Neptune) or self-hosted infrastructure with its own scaling, backup, and monitoring concerns.

## Object Sub-Pools

One concept from the current architecture that should carry forward is the **object pool** (formerly called a sub-pool) — a self-contained subgraph where outside nodes may point to the root, but all internal objects hold no hard references to objects outside the subgraph. These sub-pools can be nested and are the natural unit of ownership, sync, and access control.

In practice, sub-pools correspond to the coarse-grained "documents" of an application. In a contacts app, for example, each contact card — with its addresses, phone numbers, notes, and group memberships — forms a sub-pool. The contacts list holds references to each card's root, but the internal objects within a card don't reference objects in other cards. Each sub-pool can be:

- **Synced independently** — upload or download a sub-pool without touching the rest of the graph
- **Garbage collected** — objects reachable only within the sub-pool can be collected together
- **Access controlled** — permissions can be scoped to a sub-pool (e.g., a user owns their contacts but shares specific groups with collaborators)
- **Migrated or archived** — move a sub-pool to cold storage or a different backend without breaking references

A graph database backend should preserve this sub-pool structure as a first-class concept — not flatten everything into a single global graph. The sub-pool boundary is what makes it practical to sync, permission, and reason about parts of the graph independently, even though the database itself supports arbitrary cross-references.

## Relationship to Current Architecture

This is envisioned as a backend replacement, not a framework rewrite. The domain model, slot system, persistence API, and view layer would remain unchanged. The swap would happen below the record store protocol (`SvRecordStoreProtocol`):

- `SvLocalRecordStore` continues to manage local IndexedDB storage
- A new `SvRecordStoreProtocol` backing would speak to a graph database API instead of the records collection
- The serialization format would change from JSON documents to node/edge mutations
- The sync protocol would change from per-pool versioned commits to a graph-aware change feed
- Object sub-pools remain the unit of sync — the graph database stores the full graph, but sync, permissions, and lifecycle operate at the sub-pool level

The domain model already *is* a graph — the change is making the storage layer acknowledge that.

## Timeline

This is a long-term architectural direction, not near-term work. The current Firebase-based cloud sync is functional and sufficient for the application's current scale. A graph database backend would become compelling when:

- The object graph grows large enough that pool-level sync becomes a bottleneck
- Multi-user collaborative editing requires finer-grained conflict resolution than document-level merging
- Query patterns emerge that are awkward to express without structural graph traversal


---

<!-- Page: docs/Plans/JSON Schema -->
Source: docs/Plans/JSON%20Schema/

# JSON Schema

Expanding auto-generated JSON Schema coverage across slots, classes, and the domain model.

**Status:** slot-level keywords and validation against them are built (2026-11-17, see [What Was Built](docs/Plans/JSON%20Schema/#what-was-built)); `pattern` is checked too (2026-11-18); in the framework the only slot that declares a constraint is `SvToolCall.callId`'s pattern, and the app declared its first number bounds the same day. **Left:** the class-level keywords, type unions. Leave `if`/`then`/`else` until a real case needs it.

## Context

STRVCT automatically generates JSON Schema from the domain model — classes produce object schemas, slots produce property schemas, and cross-references between classes produce `$ref` and `definitions` entries. These schemas are used for AI tool calls (constraining function parameters), data exchange, and validation.

The current implementation covers the most common schema features, but there are gaps at both the slot level (individual property constraints) and the class level (object-wide constraints and composition). Closing these gaps would make the auto-generated schemas more precise, which directly improves AI behavior — tighter schemas reduce hallucinated parameters and improve structured output quality.

## Current Coverage

### Class-level (SvNode)

`SvNode.asJsonSchema()` generates object schemas with:

| JSON Schema keyword | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | Always `"object"` | |
| `description` | `jsonSchemaDescription()` | Static method on each class |
| `properties` | `jsonSchemaProperties()` | Composed from slots marked `isInJsonSchema` |
| `required` | `jsonSchemaRequired()` | From slots marked `isRequired` |
| `additionalProperties` | `additionalProperties()` | Boolean — whether extra keys are accepted |
| `readOnly` | `jsonSchemaIsReadOnly()` | Optional, class-wide |
| `title` | `jsonSchemaTitle()` | Only emitted when different from class name |
| `$ref` | `jsonSchemaRef()` | For cross-class references |
| `definitions` | `jsonSchemaDefinitionsForRefSet()` | Collects all referenced classes recursively |

### Slot-level (Slot)

`Slot.asJsonSchema()` generates property schemas with:

| JSON Schema keyword | Slot API | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `setSlotType()` | Mapped to JSON Schema types |
| `description` | `setDescription()` | |
| `title` | Auto-generated | From slot name |
| `default` | `initValue()` | When not `undefined` |
| `enum` | `setValidValues()` / `setValidItems()` | |
| `examples` | `setExamples()` | |
| `pattern` | `setPattern()` | String regex; checked (was `setJsonSchemaPattern()`, schema-only, until 2026-11-18) |
| `readOnly` | `setIsReadOnly()` | |
| `items` | `setJsonSchemaItemsType()` | Array item type, description, uniqueItems, $ref |
| `properties` | `setFinalInitProto()` | Nested object schemas |
| `$ref` | Auto-generated | For slots referencing node classes |

### Already inconsistent (fixed 2026-11-17)

One annotation had two readers that disagreed: `SvFieldTile` emits `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` from a slot's `minimum` / `maximum` annotations, but `Slot.asJsonSchema()` doesn't emit those annotations. It only derives `minimum` and `maximum` from a contiguous integer `enum`. Wiring the annotation into the schema is the natural first change.

## Slot-Level Keywords

All of these now have a slot setter named after the keyword (`setMinimum(n)`, `setMaxLength(n)`, …), in `Slot_constraints.js`:

### Numeric constraints

- **`minimum` / `maximum`** — bounded ranges for Number slots (e.g., ability scores 1–30, hit points 0–999)
- **`exclusiveMinimum` / `exclusiveMaximum`** — strict bounds
- **`multipleOf`** — step constraints (e.g., currency in increments of 0.01)

### String constraints

- **`minLength` / `maxLength`** — character limits for text fields
- **`pattern`** — a regular expression the string must match
- **`format`** — semantic formats like `"date-time"`, `"email"`, `"uri"`, `"uuid"`. Particularly useful for AI — knowing a string is a UUID vs. a display name changes how the AI generates it

### Array constraints

- **`minItems` / `maxItems`** — collection size bounds
- **`uniqueItems`** — partially supported on item-typed arrays but not as a general slot annotation (not added)

## Missing Class-Level Keywords

### Composition

- **`oneOf` / `anyOf` / `allOf`** — union and intersection types. A slot that accepts "either a UoCharacter or a UoCreatureTemplate" currently can't express this. At the class level, this could describe polymorphic collections.
- **`const`** — fixed-value properties (more specific than a single-element enum)

### Conditional

- **`if` / `then` / `else`** — conditional validation. For example: if `characterClass` is "Wizard" then `spellSlots` is required; if `type` is "ranged" then `range` must be present. These constraints currently live only in code or prompt text.

### Object structure

- **`propertyNames`** — constraints on key names for Map-typed slots
- **`patternProperties`** — schema for properties matching a regex pattern
- **`minProperties` / `maxProperties`** — bounds on the number of properties

## Implementation Approach (as planned)

### Slot-level additions

Each missing keyword follows the existing annotation pattern — a getter/setter pair on `Slot` that `asJsonSchema()` reads:

```javascript
// On Slot:
setMinimum (n) {
    this.setAnnotation("minimum", n);
    return this;
}

minimum () {
    return this.getAnnotation("minimum");
}

// In asJsonSchema():
const min = this.minimum();
if (min !== undefined) {
    schema.minimum = min;
}
```

The slot system's annotation mechanism already supports arbitrary key-value metadata, so no structural changes are needed — just adding the accessors and wiring them into `asJsonSchema()`.

### Class-level additions

Composition keywords (`oneOf`, `anyOf`) would need static methods on `SvNode` that `asJsonSchema()` includes in the class schema. Conditional keywords (`if`/`then`/`else`) are more complex — they'd require a way to express inter-slot dependencies at the class level, possibly as a static `jsonSchemaConditionals()` method that returns an array of condition objects.

### Validation unification

Currently, JSON Schema annotations are output-only — they describe the slot's contract to external consumers but don't enforce it at runtime. A natural extension would be to have the auto-generated setter validate against the same constraints:

- A `Number` slot with `setMinimum(0)` would reject negative values
- A `String` slot with `setMaxLength(100)` would warn on overflow
- A `String` slot with `setFormat("email")` could validate format

This would unify schema declaration and runtime validation, ensuring the contract described to AI consumers is actually enforced in the application. The existing `validatesOnSet` mechanism already provides the hook point — it just needs to consult the richer set of annotations.

**A new constraint applies to every record already stored**, the same way slot flags do. So it must never stop a record loading:

- **Loading** (`loadFromRecord`, `deserializeFromJson`, lazy materialization): warn and keep the value. The setter already only warns on a type mismatch; constraints should do the same.
- **Edits** (the user, a JSON patch from an AI): reject, with a message built from the annotation ("must be at least 0"). For AI patches the rejection goes back as a tool-call error, so the model can correct itself.
- **Field tiles** show the same message beside the field, which is the Data Validation idea from Emergent Capabilities: one set of annotations feeding the schema, the ARIA attributes and the error text.

## What Was Built

2026-11-17. `Slot_constraints.js`, a category of `Slot`, with `tests/headless/TestSlotConstraints.js`.

| Constraint | Applies to | Schema | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setMinimum` / `setMaximum` | Number | yes | yes |
| `setExclusiveMinimum` / `setExclusiveMaximum` | Number | yes | yes |
| `setMultipleOf` | Number | yes | yes, allowing for floating point |
| `setMinLength` / `setMaxLength` | String | yes | yes |
| `setPattern` | String | yes | yes (2026-11-18) |
| `setMinItems` / `setMaxItems` | Array | yes | yes |
| `setFormat` | String | yes | no |

One declaration has four readers:

- **The schema.** `Slot.asJsonSchema()` emits each declared keyword. A declared `maxLength` never raises the 16 KB cap a stored string already has.
- **The error sentence.** `slot.constraintErrorForValue(v)` returns "Must be at most 20." or `null`. It judges only the constraints for the value's type; the slot's type check is separate.
- **ARIA.** `SvFieldTile` reads `slot.minimum()` / `slot.maximum()`, the same values the schema emits.
- **The setter**, which warns and keeps the value.

Where an edit is refused:

- **A field.** `SvField.validateValue(v)` now returns the target slot's sentence (`SvField.targetSlot()` finds the slot), and `SvNumberField` adds it to its own checks. The field tile already showed a field's error and held the value back from the model, so nothing changed in the view.
- **A JSON patch.** The preflight refuses the whole batch before anything is applied, for the patched slot and for a field inside a value being added, with the sentence in the error the AI gets back.

Decisions made along the way:

- **The setter cannot refuse.** It can't tell a load from an edit, so the refusal lives where edits come in. Code that calls a setter directly with a bad value gets a warning, not an error.
- **The patch refusal assumes patches are edits.** Today the only caller of `applyJsonPatches` is the AI's `patchClientState` tool. If patches are ever used again to copy state from one machine to another, that path must skip the constraint check, or a value that loaded with a warning on the host would be refused on the client.
- **`format` is not checked.** It tells the AI what kind of string to write; checking each format is a separate piece of work.
- **`pattern` is checked (2026-11-18).** `setJsonSchemaPattern`, which predated this and was only emitted, became `setPattern`, one of the constraints: its sentence is "Must match the pattern ^call_\d+$", which suits an AI better than a person, and a malformed pattern throws where it is declared. Its one declarer is `SvToolCall.callId`, so a call id of another shape now warns in the setter (and is kept).
- **`SvNumberField`'s own `minValue` / `maxValue`** (used by sliders) are left as they are. A slot's `minimum` / `maximum` could feed them, which would retire the pair.

**No slot declares a constraint yet apart from `SvToolCall.callId`'s pattern**, in the framework or the app, so nothing else behaves differently until one does. The app's first ones (2026-11-18) showed how to add them: scan the stored data for the slot first. A proposed minimum of 1 was found to be wrong for two stored records where 0 meant "at will", and the bound became 0; the app's test now checks every stored JSON file against whatever bounds are declared. Each one added is a decision about data already stored (it will warn on load) and about what the AI may write (it will be refused), so they are best added where a wrong value has been seen.

## Richer Type Unions

Slots currently declare a single type via `setSlotType("String")`. Some slots legitimately accept multiple types — a value that could be a `String` or `null`, or a slot that holds either a `Number` or an `Array`. The type system doesn't express this, leading to validation warnings that must be suppressed.

A possible API:

```javascript
slot.setSlotType("String|null");
// or:
slot.setSlotTypes(["String", "Number"]);
```

This would generate `oneOf` or union types in JSON Schema and validate against any of the listed types at runtime.

## Open Questions

- Should all JSON Schema keywords be supported, or only those that map to runtime behavior? Keywords like `if`/`then`/`else` add schema expressiveness but may be complex to implement as runtime validation.
- How should schema versioning work? If the schema changes between app versions, should the schema include a `$id` with a version component?
- Could the framework auto-infer some constraints — for example, deriving `minimum: 0` from a slot named "count" or "quantity"? Or is explicit annotation always better?
- How should the schema handle slots that are writable by the app but read-only for AI? The current `readOnly` is all-or-nothing.

<!-- Page: docs/Plans/Lazy Slots -->
Source: docs/Plans/Lazy%20Slots/

# Lazy Slots

Deferring object loading until first access, so large object graphs don't pay for what they don't touch.

**Status:** shipped (2026-07), with a few items left (below). In use by app collections and character sheet sections; `tests/headless/TestLazyMaterializationNeutrality.js` and `TestPendingMaterialization.js` cover it.

## What Shipped

A stored slot marked lazy isn't loaded with its owner. It holds a placeholder until something reads it:

```javascript
{
    const slot = this.newSlot("locations", null);
    slot.setShouldStoreSlot(true);
    slot.setIsLazy(true);
}
```

- **Loading leaves a placeholder.** `loadFromRecord` puts an `SvStoreRef` (the record's pid) in the slot instead of instantiating the object and everything it reaches.
- **The getter is synchronous.** The record store reads a pool's records into memory when it opens, so turning a pid into an object needs no I/O, and the first getter call does it in place: `onInstanceMaterializeLazySlot` loads the object through the pool (whose identity map keeps one instance per pid) and writes it through the setter, so slot hooks and view sync fire as for any other change. No caller awaits anything. The objection in `SvStorableNode` ("no point in using this until we have coroutines") no longer applies.
- **Loading is not editing.** A write that replaces an `SvStoreRef` is a load, so it marks nothing dirty and touches no timestamps. Hooks can tell: `oldValue instanceof SvStoreRef` means "there was no previous live value". `Slot.isMaterializingAnyLazySlot()` covers the one consumer that can't see the old value.
- **Untouched subtrees round-trip.** Serializing a slot that still holds its `SvStoreRef` writes the pid back without loading it.
- **Lazy collections.** Laziness is per slot, not per array element: a collection is lazy as a whole (`subnodes` included), and a deep tree gets a lazy boundary at each level.
- **A default for lazy slots with a proto.** A lazy slot with no stored value creates its `finalInitProto` default on first access rather than at load (`onInstanceMaterializeLazyDefault`).
- **JSON too.** Reading JSON into a node parks the JSON for a lazy slot in an `SvLazyJsonRef`, so importing a large object doesn't build subtrees nobody looks at.
- **Failure.** If the record is missing, the getter returns null or the owner's `onFailedLazyLoadSlot<Name>()` fallback. The `SvStoreRef` stays in the slot, so the next access retries (rate-limited by a negative cache on the ref), and a fallback written by the hook is a load, not a repair, so it isn't stored. An exception while deserializing propagates; it is a bug, not a missing record.
- **GC.** Store GC marks reachable records by walking records, not instances, so unloaded subtrees stay reachable. Blob GC scans records for hashes for the same reason.

The design and its measurements (boot went from 12.5 s to 8.3 s, with two-thirds of a mature store left unloaded) are in undreamedof.ai's "Slot Lazy Loading" plan.

## What Changes for Code in a Lazy Subtree

- `finalInit()` and `afterInit()` of a lazily held object run when it loads, not at boot. Nothing outside the subtree may rely on them having run.
- Observers inside the subtree don't exist until it loads, so the subtree registers its own when it wakes.
- `duplicate()` loads the value: copying is an explicit "I need it" moment.

## What Remains

- **Why records go missing.** The failure handling is containment; the cause of the missing records it was built for hasn't been found.
- **Docs.** This belongs in the Persistence docs (Local Object Pools) as a description, with this page reduced to the remaining items.
- **Old scaffolding.** The commented-out `setIsLazy(true)` in `SvStorableNode` and its comment, and the commented-out `hasBeenLoaded` slot in `SvJsonGroup`, predate this design and can go.
- **Choosing what to make lazy.** Today it's per slot, chosen from a histogram of records by class. A framework default (for example, lazy subnodes for every windowed or pool-backed collection) hasn't been considered.

## Relationship to Other Plans

- [Async Final Initialization](docs/Plans/Async%20Final%20Initialization/) was the other answer to "an object isn't ready yet". Synchronous materialization removed its main case.
- [Promise-Wrapped Slots](docs/Plans/Promise-Wrapped%20Slots/) cache values that are *computed* asynchronously; lazy slots defer *loading* stored ones. They don't overlap now that loading is synchronous.
- [Async Navigation](docs/Plans/Async%20Navigation/) assumed lazy loading would be async. It isn't, which removes one of its motivations.

# Meta Plan

The order to do the other plans in, why, and what should change in them first.

**As of:** 2026-11-23. Every plan page opens with a status line; this page orders them. Steps 1 to 6 are built: 1 to 3 done, 4 (Capabilities & Permissions) and 5's first part (slot constraints) seen working in a browser on 2026-11-19, and 6 (Browser Cleanup) built in all four parts, its compaction coordinator released to production on 2026-11-22. On 2026-11-23 the plans were checked against the code: Browser Cleanup's composable breadcrumbs and auxiliary view had been built on 2026-06-12, as `SvBreadCrumbsView` and the companion, and the plan had not noticed. The steps below follow from that check; all four were built on 2026-11-23, and only a VoiceOver listen is left.

## Next Steps

Chosen 2026-11-23, in this order. The 2026-11-18 set (A to C) is [below](docs/Plans/Meta%20Plan/#done-the-2026-11-18-steps).

### 1. Put back what the 2026-11-23 check found broken or stale — done (2026-11-23)

Small, and each is a fault a reader or a user can meet today. All done the same day: the breadcrumbs' `aria-current` (with `TestBreadCrumbsAriaCurrent`), the Responsive page rewritten around claims and `SvLayerAllocation`, and the stale class name replaced.

- **The breadcrumb bar's `aria-current`.** `SvBreadCrumbsTile` set `aria-current="location"` on the last crumb; `SvBreadCrumbsView`, which replaced it on 2026-06-12, does not. Put it back, with a headless check.
- **Docs that describe code that is gone.** [Responsive](docs/Views/Responsive/) explains compaction with `compactNavAsNeeded` and `updateWidthForWindow`, both removed by the compaction coordinator; rewrite it around claims and `SvLayerAllocation`. [Accessibility](docs/Accessibility/), [Internationalization](docs/Internationalization/) and [Auto-Generated Views](docs/Views/Auto-Generated%20Views/) still name `SvBreadCrumbsTile`.

### 2. Keep the framework free of app names (was B) — done (2026-11-23)

**Built:** `TestUndefinedClassNames` fails when framework code uses a name as a class (`extends`, `new`, `instanceof`, `.clone()`, `.shared()`, a slot type, `SvGlobals.get`) that no framework file defines, that is not a platform API, and that is not listed with its reason. It found no app names, and two real faults, both fixed: an audio file read through `SvResourceFile` made an `SvSoundResource`, a class that never existed (seen decoding to an `SvWaSound` in a browser after the fix), and a slot type spelled `"NumbeStringr"`. It does not read prose in strings, so it could not see the prompt example below. **The prompt example** (Steve chose a neutral one, 2026-11-23): `SvToolDefinitions` now shows a made-up `addNote` tool, marked as not in the model's list; the game's own `rollRequest` examples stay in its prompt files (`DiceRollToolPrompt.txt`), and an assertion that the framework's prompt mentioned `rollRequest` is gone. Three comments still name `rollRequest` as an example of a tool that waits for the user.

What was planned: the ratchet test, like `TestPlatformGlobalsInModels`: fail when framework code references a class that no framework file defines. It needs no app prefix, so it stays general, and it stops the drift the 2026-11-18 cleanup undid. One known use stays until Steve chooses: the tool instructions every AI conversation receives (`SvToolDefinitions`) use the app's `rollRequest` and `UoRollRequestMessage` as their worked example. The recommendation is a neutral example made up for the framework, with the game keeping its own in its prompt files; it changes the game's prompt, so it waits on that choice. Details in [Naked Objects Issues](docs/Plans/Naked%20Objects%20Issues/#app-names-in-framework-code).

### 3. Navigation announcements, with the entry point's second pass — built (2026-11-23), not yet heard with VoiceOver

**Built:** a model's focus notes are selected on behalf of a `"program"` request, and a browser says the title of a place code moved the user to, through one polite live region (`SvLiveAnnouncer`). Checked headless (`TestNavigationEntryPoint`) and in Chromium against `just launch` (`tests/e2e/navigation-announcements.spec.js`, new; `navigation-entry-point` and `meta-plan-step-a` still pass). Still to do: listen with VoiceOver. See [Accessibility Testing & Tuning](docs/Plans/Accessibility%20Testing%20%26%20Tuning/#navigation-announcement-mechanism).

What was planned:

The first feature in [Accessibility Testing & Tuning](docs/Plans/Accessibility%20Testing%20%26%20Tuning/#navigation-announcement-mechanism), and the last open part of Browser Cleanup. A path change now says who caused it, so announcing a `"program"` navigation is a listener and a live region. It is right only once the focus-and-expand notes and the other unrequested path changes go through `navigate()` ([second pass](docs/Plans/Browser%20Cleanup/#second-pass-open)); today they are recorded as the user's and would go unannounced. Checked in a browser with VoiceOver, not only headless.

### 4. Tile Container Views: the wrapping grid — built (2026-11-23)

**Built** as recommended and agreed (2026-11-23): a node answers `nodeChildrenLayout()` `"grid"`; `SvTilesView_grid` lays its tiles out as cells that wrap, fills whenever shown, moves by arrow keys in two dimensions, and reorders by drag with the cells kept in the grid. A character's (and a location's, and a trap's) artwork is the first user. Checked headless (`TestTilesViewGrid`) and in Chromium (`tests/e2e/artwork-grid.spec.js`). The grid's drag found that **reordering any list by drag had been broken**: the placeholder's slot type refused the placeholder, and the drop handed `setSubnodes()` a plain Array, which a subclass's slot refused after the moved node had been removed, so the node was lost. Both fixed, with a list check in the same spec. See [Tile Container Views](docs/Plans/Tile%20Container%20Views/#the-first-grid-built-2026-11-23).

What was planned: `setNodeTilesViewClass()` and the first grid. It waits on nothing (decided 2026-11-20), and the manual accessibility passes and the Photo Gallery case study wait on it. Its ARIA roles come with it.

### Not next

More slot constraints are declared where a wrong value is seen, not as a project (each is a decision about stored data). The two hand-kept promises in [Cleanup Notes](docs/Plans/Cleanup%20Notes/#hand-kept-promises) wait until their files are changed. Promise-wrapped slots wait for a first user. The rest of the compaction coordinator's part D, and the companion's missing hints, wait for a case that needs them. A review of compaction parts C and D, which shipped without one, is welcome whenever a reviewer is free; its questions are in [For the next pass](docs/Plans/Compaction%20Coordinator/#for-the-next-pass).

### Done: the 2026-11-18 steps

- **A. A browser pass over steps 2 to 5** (2026-11-19). Run against `just launch` and the deployed dev project, in Playwright specs that cost nothing to rerun: `hosted-table-invite-signup`, `meta-plan-step-a`, `editability-browser-pass` and `editability-views-browser-pass`. It found and fixed an empty catalog under `just launch` (since 2026-11-13) and Cmd+D duplicating into a read-only list; `TestEditabilityInViews` now also fails on a view method that changes a node's list without asking. It showed that a player cannot reach the catalog's nodes or a character's raw number fields by hand, so for players the view refusals and a field's error sentence are a second line behind the server's refusal and the patch preflight. **Still unseen:** a failed fetch from Cloud Storage rather than the local pool (needs a deployed project), and the narrated-sentence highlight during real narration.
- **B. App names.** Carried forward as step 2 above.
- **C. One navigation entry point** (2026-11-19). `SvBrowserView.navigate(aRequest)`; see [Browser Cleanup](docs/Plans/Browser%20Cleanup/#one-navigation-entry-point). The compaction coordinator followed it and was released 2026-11-22.

## Recommended Order

### 1. A test runner — done (2026-11-15)

`npm test` (or `just test`) rebuilds `build/_index.json`, then runs every `tests/headless/Test*.js` in its own process, one at a time, with a timeout each; arguments filter by file name (`npm test -- Record`). The tests share LevelDB databases under `data/leveldb/`, so they can't run in parallel. The first full run found one flaky test, `TestWindowedCollections`: classic-level's `close()` resolves before LevelDB lets go of its files, so a quick reopen sometimes failed. `SvIndexedDbFolder` now retries such an open briefly, and the test's sleeps are gone. All tests pass (73 then; 80 after steps 2 and 3), in under a minute.

### 2. The model/view boundary — done (2026-11-15)

[Naked Objects Issues](docs/Plans/Naked%20Objects%20Issues/): add the environment accessors and view actions, move the nine classes onto them, then add the ratchet test. The list is short, and the headless and swappable-UI claims depend on it.

**App names (2026-11-18), the boundary's other side.** The framework must not know the app, and an audit found it did in a few places: a dead `session()` that looked up `UoSession`, a default tile named `UoChatInputTile`, an error message naming `UoBuildEnv`, and app classes used as examples in comments and a test fixture. All gone (strvct `9bf3aadd`), except the prompt example in next step B.

### 3. Runtime-risk fixes — done (2026-11-15)

- `markPid()` is iterative ([Cleanup Notes](docs/Plans/Cleanup%20Notes/#can-fail-at-runtime)).
- A promise-wrapped slot's cached promise is cleared when it fails ([Promise-Wrapped Slots](docs/Plans/Promise-Wrapped%20Slots/#error-recovery)). Its getter had never worked; the feature was then finished properly (one promise every caller shares), though nothing uses it yet.

The rest of Cleanup Notes is for when a file is being changed anyway.

**Shared promises (2026-11-15), which came out of this step.** Finishing the slot feature raised the question of the code that hand-kept a `fooPromise` for work several callers ask for at once. An audit of those copies found each had something wrong (a failure cached forever, a retry that never ran, a finished run clearing a newer one, an unhandled second rejection, work that carried on after being abandoned). `Object_sharedPromises.js` now gives every object three helpers (once, one at a time, fresh), and 23 hand-written copies in the framework and the app moved onto them. See [Async Patterns](docs/Programming%20Idioms/Async%20Patterns/index.html). Two framework copies are left, listed in [Cleanup Notes](docs/Plans/Cleanup%20Notes/#hand-kept-promises).

### 4. Capabilities & Permissions — built (2026-11-17), seen in a browser (2026-11-19)

The most user-facing value: the failure it describes is silent data loss. **Its first step is done (2026-11-16):** titles, drags in and out, reordering, desktop drops and three field paths now ask the cascade, a refused drop says so, and `TestEditabilityInViews` fails on a view that reads a raw capability.

**The rest followed (2026-11-17).** The server now tells the client, with every read, whether the caller may write; the cloud store remembers it and a document's pool carries it into the cascade, so the views and the commit cannot disagree. A commit refused for permission reloads the cloud's copy and tells the user. The work found that the client had been discarding the server's error codes, so no refusal was ever recognized as one. Not done, by decision: separate read, delete, share and create hooks, and a live push of role changes.

### 5. JSON Schema and validation

Additive, and tighter schemas improve AI tool calls at once. Start by emitting the `minimum` / `maximum` annotations that the ARIA code already reads.

**Slot constraints — done (2026-11-17).** Ten setters on `Slot`, named after their JSON Schema keywords, with four readers: the schema, the error sentence a field shows, ARIA, and the setter's warning. An AI patch that breaks one is refused before anything is applied. See [JSON Schema](docs/Plans/JSON%20Schema/#what-was-built). `pattern` joined them on 2026-11-18 (`setPattern`, replacing the schema-only `setJsonSchemaPattern`). The app declared its first bounds the same day, after scanning its stored data for values outside them. What remains is declaring more where a wrong value is seen (each is a decision about stored data), and the class-level keywords and type unions when a case needs them.

### 6. Browser Cleanup — built

One navigation entry point (2026-11-19); the compaction coordinator (released 2026-11-22); composable breadcrumbs and the auxiliary view, which turned out to have been built on 2026-06-12 as `SvBreadCrumbsView` and the companion. The entry point's second pass is left, and goes with the navigation announcements (next step 3).

### 7. Tile Container Views and Tile Views

The wrapping grid is built (step 4 above). The table, scrolling over windowed collections, and the list/grid switcher are next when a case needs them. Meter and badge tiles can be done at any point.

### 8. Accessibility

The navigation announcements are built (step 3), not yet heard with VoiceOver. The manual passes can start: the first grid is built (step 7).

### 9. Case Studies

Contacts can run as early as step 2, as a gap-finder; what it finds comes back to this page. The rest once their features exist.

## Not Yet Plans

- **The [First Principles](docs/First%20Principles/) essay** is on hold (2026-11-23) until after the Thanksgiving break, or when Steve has time. He edits it by hand first, then asks for help.

- **Undo / redo** has no other home. Write it as its own plan when wanted, built on slot-change notifications and `pool.transaction()`.
- **Schema migration.** Class renames are handled (`classNameConversionMap()`); slot type changes and custom migrations aren't. Write a plan when a real type change needs it, taking in the migration item from Emergent Capabilities.
- **Choosing lazy slots by default** (from [Lazy Slots](docs/Plans/Lazy%20Slots/#what-remains)): whether windowed or pool-backed collections should be lazy without being asked.

<!-- Page: docs/Plans/Naked Objects Issues -->
Source: docs/Plans/Naked%20Objects%20Issues/

# Naked Objects Issues

Known places where framework model classes still cross the model/view boundary — touching view classes, browser globals, or UI state — plus the framework gaps that force such crossings.

**Status:** done for framework model code (2026-11-15): every class below is moved, and the ratchet test's baseline is empty. Two gaps remain open (a viewport accessor, a platform client id); close them when a model needs them. App class names were taken out of framework code on 2026-11-18 ([below](docs/Plans/Naked%20Objects%20Issues/#app-names-in-framework-code)); `TestUndefinedClassNames` keeps them out (2026-11-23); the prompt example was made neutral (2026-11-23). The browser-side changes were seen working in the app on 2026-11-19 (Meta Plan, step A).

The target is the model/view separation and **Platform Abstraction** rules in the framework guide (see [App Lifecycle](docs/Lifecycle/App%20Lifecycle/index.html)): a model (`SvNode` and subclasses) should never reach into `document` / `window` / `navigator` / `localStorage` or reference view classes, so it stays headless-clean and the UI platform stays swappable.

## Framework model classes still touching the platform

| Class | What it does | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SvErrorReport` | Read `navigator.userAgent`, `window.location`, `document.referrer` for a report | **Done:** `SvPlatform.userAgent()`, `pageUrl()`, `referrer()` |
| `SvFirestoreNode` | Read `window.location.hostname` and set a `window.__uo_firestore_emulator_configured__` flag | **Done:** the host from `SvPlatform.pageUrl()`; the configured databases in a `WeakSet` on the class |
| `SvAiParsedResponseMessage_parsing` | `document.createElement("div")` to find tags in HTML content | **Done:** the code was already commented out; deleted |
| `SvFirebaseFile` | `window.open(url)` | **Done:** posts `onRequestOpenUrl({ url })`; the user interface's `openUrl()` opens it (headless logs it) |
| `SvOpenAiStyleTransfer` | Built a file `<input>` to pick an image | **Done:** `await userInterface().asyncPickFile({ accept })` — a `File`, or null when the user cancels (the old code never settled on cancel) |
| `SvDefaultProxyServer` | Read `window.location` for its default config | **Done:** `configDictForPageUrl(SvPlatform.pageUrl())` |
| `SvApp.hardReloadForDataReset()` | `window.location.reload()` (guarded, no-op headless) | **Done:** the user interface's `reloadApp()` |
| `SvXhrRequest` | Read `window.location.protocol` to explain a failed request from `file:` | **Done:** `SvPlatform.pageUrl()` (null headless) |
| `SvgIconNode.svgIconView()` | Created an `SvgIconView` (its own TODO said so) | **Done:** it and `SvIconResources.iconWithName()` were unused — `SvgIconView.setIconName()` already finds the node; both deleted |
| `SvApp` | `localStorage` for the clear-on-boot flag, accepted reset epochs and boot store stats | **Done:** the user interface's `deviceValue()`. The web UI adopts a value still stored under its bare key (the old format) and moves it, so a pending flag or an accepted epoch survives; `tests/headless/TestDeviceValues.js` covers it |
| `SvErrorImageResolver` | Read `window.location.origin` | **Done:** `SvPlatform.pageUrl()` |

`SvResourceManager` also reads `sessionStorage`, but it runs at boot, below the model layer, so it is outside this rule.

## Framework gaps to close

These abstractions would let model code — framework *and* app — stay on the right side of the boundary:

- **Environment info** — **done:** `SvPlatform.pageUrl()` (a `URL`, null headless), `userAgent()` and `referrer()`. On `SvPlatform` rather than the user interface: it lives in boot, so it is there before `SvApp` exists (an error report at boot needs it), and models already ask it `isOnline()`.
- **Platform-provided client/device id** — one environment accessor instead of each model reading `sessionStorage`.
- **View-layer actions** — **done:** open a URL (`onRequestOpenUrl` note → `openUrl()`), pick a file (`asyncPickFile()`), write to the clipboard (`asyncCopyText()`, already there). A download is an open URL until something needs more.
- **Reload** — **done:** the user interface's `reloadApp()` (it existed; `SvApp` now uses it).
- **Viewport accessor** — models that need size should receive it from the view rather than reading `window.innerWidth` / `devicePixelRatio`.
- **User alerts** — already available: post `onRequestUserAlert` and the UI presents it (panel in the browser, log headless). Models should use it instead of `window.alert`.

Closing these unblocks the same cleanups in any app built on STRVCT.

## Keeping it from coming back

**Done:** `tests/headless/TestPlatformGlobalsInModels.js` scans `source/library/` (skipping `view/`, `node_views/`, `node/app/ui/`, `browser-only/` and `_unused/`, and comments) for `window.`, `navigator.`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and `document.` followed by a DOM member, so a local variable called `document` doesn't count. It fails on any use its baseline (`tests/headless/fixtures/platformGlobalsInModels.json`) doesn't list, and says when the baseline can shrink.

Low-level platform utilities are not model code reading UI state, and the test's `ALLOWED` table lists them with a reason each: canvas work in `Image_ideal`, `SvImageBorderRemover` and `SvImageMosaic`; HTML parsing in `String_ideal`; `AudioContext` in `SvSimpleSynth` and `SvWaContext`; `document.fonts` in `SvFont`; DOM output in `SvHtmlStreamReader`. Two had a native global that works in both environments and moved to it: `Object_puuid` uses `globalThis.crypto` and `String_ideal` uses `btoa` / `atob` (which threw headless before). Nothing was reimplemented.

## App names in framework code

The same boundary seen from the other side: the framework must not know the app built on it. An audit on 2026-11-18 found app class names in framework code. Fixed in strvct `9bf3aadd`:

- `SvAiParsedResponseMessage_voiceNarration.session()` looked up the app's global `UoSession`, a ReferenceError under any other app or headless. Nothing called it, and the app's response message defines its own; removed.
- `SvAiParsedResponseMessage` set the app's `UoChatInputTile` as its tile. Removed; it inherits `SvChatMessageTile`, which behaves the same for it (the app tile's one addition, applying `cssVariableDict()`, does nothing for a node that returns none). The app's response message still sets its own tile.
- `SvFirebaseStorageService` kept a commented-out `UoBuildEnv` block, and its missing-bucket error named it (and said "found" for not found).
- About 30 comments, and the record-store test fixture's type names, used app classes as examples; they now use generic ones.

**The prompt example — neutral (2026-11-23).** The tool instructions every AI conversation receives (`SvToolDefinitions`, "How to Use These Definitions") used the app's `rollRequest` tool and `#/definitions/UoRollRequestMessage` as the worked example. Steve chose a neutral example over one built from the first real tool: it is a made-up `addNote` tool, marked as not in the model's list. The game's own `rollRequest` examples were already in its prompt files. `SvAssistantToolKit.formalToolSpecificationsPrompt()` (unused) asserted the prompt mentioned `rollRequest`; that assertion is gone. Three comments still use `rollRequest` as an example of a tool that waits for the user.

**The ratchet test — built 2026-11-23.** `tests/headless/TestUndefinedClassNames.js` fails on any name framework code uses as a class (`extends X`, `new X(`, `instanceof X`, `X.clone()` / `X.shared()` / `X.prototype`, `setSlotType("X")`, `SvGlobals.get("X")`, `setFinalInitProto(X)`) that no framework file defines and that is not a platform API. It names no app prefix, so it would catch another app's names as well as this one's. It has no baseline: its first run found no app names, and two real faults, both fixed (an audio file read through `SvResourceFile` made an `SvSoundResource`, a class that never existed; a slot type was spelled `"NumbeStringr"`). Comments and prose in strings are not read, so the prompt example above was found by reading, and comments are left to review.
